page: Amazon Web Services r5n.metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture. It features a custom Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz, providing 48 physical cores and 96 dedicated hardware threads without hypervisor overhead. The hardware includes AVX-512 with VNNI support, 35 MB of L3 cache, and direct access to virtualization primitives via Intel VMX. The platform is configured with 768 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, offering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio suited for memory-intensive architectures.

The server delivers high-throughput network connectivity with a baseline bandwidth of 100 Gbps. It contains no bundled local NVMe storage, meaning all persistence relies on remote Elastic Block Store volumes or network-attached systems. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate top-quartile results across memory bandwidth tests, achieving 224.16 GB/s on large uncached reads and 4545.42 GB/s on small cached reads. Multi-core compute performance is robust, highlighted by a PassMark CPU score of 57,382.97 and strong parallel compilation throughput.

With 77.09 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and high database operation scores, r5n.metal is efficient for large in-memory caching systems, distributed databases, and high-bandwidth data shuffling pipelines. The lack of integrated GPUs and modest single-thread CPU performance make it unsuitable for machine learning generation tasks, while its lack of local storage requires architectural planning around network I/O for persistent disk performance.
description: Amazon Web Services r5n.metal is a bare-metal memory-optimized instance featuring dual Intel Xeon 8259CL processors delivering 48 physical cores and 96 execution threads at 3.1 GHz. Configured with 768 GB of DDR4 system memory and 100 Gbps baseline networking, it bypasses hypervisor virtualization layers to maximize memory and network throughput. Benchmark results show strong performance in multi-core compute, uncached memory bandwidth (224.16 GB/s), and in-memory key-value processing, reaching 77.09 million operations per second in Redis benchmarks. Because the instance contains no integrated local storage or hardware accelerators, persistent data relies entirely on remote network storage. This profile matches high-throughput enterprise databases, in-memory caches, big data processing clusters, and network-intensive data pipeline applications.
